terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: A precast highway median segment: one solid block, nothing opens, turns or swings, nothing attaches, so one root pivot and zero sockets is the whole contract. It tiles end to end, so the butt ends are flat and square and the draw-call ceiling is the design constraint. Highway medians, expressway works, checkpoint chicanes; placed in runs of dozens. Tan-grey concrete, paler on the capping, olive-dark grime and growth along the foot, tyre scuffs on the slope, air-bubble pinholes over every cast face.

reasoning: The section is extruded along the length in TWO parts split at the slope nose -- the near-vertical upper face and the lower slope carry separate albedos, because the harness lights them differently and on one albedo the face rendered 10% dark against the plate while the slope was already right. The toe below the notch ceiling is FOUR more extrusions, one per span between the three drainage notches, so the notches are real gaps on the silhouette rather than dark plates painted on the lip. The cap is two stacked plan-with-holes extrusions -- an overhanging step and a chamfered one above it. All of it merges on one material: ONE draw call.
One material: precast concrete as a vertex colour on white, the pockets and notches darker tints, wear as one grime canvas.
No repetition system: the two pocket floors, the key tongue and the groove are four boxes in one merge; the three notches are absences, not parts.
Action readiness: one root pivot, zero sockets, one box collider on the root, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: The identity is the section -- lip, 55-degree slope, vertical face -- the two pockets in the top, and the three notches under the toe. All three are built as geometry: the pockets are holes in both cap steps, the notches are gaps between four toe extrusions, and every arris carries a 7-12 mm chamfer, because a precast unit is cast against a chamfer strip and a razor edge is the single loudest thing that says CAD rather than concrete.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: Jersey section: lip, slope, vertical face
two rectangular lifting pockets in the top

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 2.00 x 0.80 x 0.60 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=4000 triangles, <=4 draw calls, <=3 materials, <=6 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot plus 0 named mechanism pivot(s); zero sockets; box collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

silhouette.description: A 2.00 m block with a Jersey section: 0.60 m foot with a 0.09 m vertical lip, a slope to 0.311 m wide at 0.33 m, a near-vertical face to 0.224 m wide at 0.755 m, then a capping that overhangs it to 0.252 m and steps back to 0.226 m at 0.80 m. Three 0.20 m drainage notches cut the toe away to 0.07 m at x = -0.66, 0 and +0.66; two 0.13 x 0.062 m pockets go through both cap steps at x +-0.62; a 0.075 m key tongue stands 12 mm proud of one end.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x spans -1.012..+1.002: the 2.00 m declared length plus a 12 mm key tongue on the -X end (the +X end carries the matching groove); y 0.00 to 0.80; z +-0.30 at the foot, the DECLARED 0.60 m. The toe is cut away below y = 0.070 over three 0.20 m spans; the capping runs 0.755 to 0.788 at half-depth 0.126 and 0.788 to 0.800 at 0.113, so it OVERHANGS the 0.112 half-depth upper face by 14 mm and steps back again at its own top edge, which is what the plate shows. The proxy normalises to w:h:d 1:0.397:0.330 -- 0.79 m tall and 0.66 m deep at 2.00 m -- and its half-depth profile (scratch/_mon/profile.mjs) gives the section: 0.33 to 0.12 H, 0.30 at 0.15, 0.25 at 0.22, 0.20 at 0.28, 0.16 at 0.35, then 0.15 -> 0.12 to the top. Scaled by 0.60/0.66 that is the section built: a vertical lip to 0.10 m, a slope to half-depth 0.155 at 0.32 m, a near-vertical face to 0.112 at the top.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate normalises to w:h:d 1:0.397:0.330. Band table: mean |delta width| 0.024, |delta depth| 0.036 of height; the depth residual in bands 0-3 is the declared 0.60 m against the proxy 0.66 (0.078 H at the foot), the width residual is the proxy's rounded ends.

viewEvidence.note: NOT DIRECTLY OBSERVED. Confidence 0.92: a Jersey barrier is symmetric about its length by design (proxy d/w 0.330 both sides); the back face is the front face.

componentTree.name: Precast concrete segment
componentTree.topologyRationale: One extruded section, one pocketed slab and nine small boxes merged into one geometry on one material: one draw call.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Section polygon (z, y) split at the slope nose and extruded 2.00 m along X above y = 0.070; the toe below that in four spans, leaving three 0.20 m notches at x = -0.66, 0, +0.66; capping as two plan-with-holes extrusions, 0.126 half-depth to 0.788 and 0.113 to 0.800, both carrying two 0.13 x 0.062 pockets at x +-0.62; pocket floors 2 mm above the body top.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: The toe overlaps the body above it by 2 mm and the upper face overlaps the lower slope by 2 mm, so no two solids share a plane; the capping sits on the body top as an OPPOSED butt joint and OVERHANGS it, so its underside is exposed rather than flush; the tongue and the groove stand 0.8-12 mm proud of the end faces. check-coplanar clean at 0.001 m.
geometryDescriptor.mergeNote: One merged BufferGeometry with height UVs at 0.8 m.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Tan as vertex colour on white concrete with a grime canvas; top slab #bfa887; pockets and notches #5e5040.

pivot.name: root
pivot.notes: At the origin the asset declares. A STATIC prop: nothing opens, turns or swings, so one root pivot is the whole mechanism inventory and that is the correct answer, not a gap.

collider.notes: Declared on the asset as box: one proxy over the whole segment, which is what a median run collides as.

roughness.notes: Scalar observed for this surface in the plate. The independently extracted map is kept on disk as evidence and is NOT bound at runtime -- this material is textureless, so the scalar is the runtime value.

albedo.samplingNotes: Measured as the mean of crops/face.png. extract_pbr_evidence confidence 0.860. The extractor palette is advisory only: these crops are flat material swatches, not isolated objects, so its foreground separation is weak by its own warnings. Albedo is the direct crop measurement.

localOverrides.evidence: crops/grime.png -- #8a7453 sd 40 at the foot; the olive-dark wash is multiplied in by the canvas over the bottom 30% of height.

evidence: Measured on viewEvidence region-face (0.86) at #a58763, sd 9. The albedo authored is NOT that value: the grime canvas is a multiply and the harness key light adds a large constant, so the transfer was probed over two albedos per surface (R = 0.74A + 41 on the upper face, R = 0.75A + 50 on the slope) and its inverse authored. Upper face #9b815f, lower slope #a88a67, capping #bea786.

Verified against the plate over matched crops: upper face renders luma 135.7 sd 10.6 against the plate's 139.6 sd 12.3, slope 154.6 against 157.3, capping 178.5 against 177.5. The first build rendered the face at 146.7 with sd 5.9 -- right hue, half the spread, which is what reads as painted rather than cast.
Textureless as DECLARED: a 512 px grime canvas after construction carrying the wash, 900 pinholes, 5 tyre scuffs, one form seam and 44 cloud patches.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

reviewHistory.summary: Material pass: one concrete at PBR confidence 0.86, textureless, albedo SOLVED rather than copied -- the harness transfer was probed over two albedos per surface (R = 0.74A + 41 on the upper face, R = 0.75A + 50 on the slope) and its inverse authored, which is why the shipped hexes are lighter than the plate's measured #a58763.
The face was flat: rendered sd 5.9 against the plate's 12.3. Added air-bubble pinholes, swept tyre scuffs over the band traffic reaches, a form seam per 0.8 m and broad cloud mottling.
The first pinholes were authored at 8 mm and the face read as gravel; a bubble is a PIN hole, so the count carries it and not the size -- 900 at ~1 mm.

The cloud mottling was sized at 0.22-0.62 of the tile, and a tile that repeats 2.5 times across the prop then repeats its clouds visibly: it read as camouflage with the seam showing. Cut to 0.04-0.17.

featureReviews.evidence: Two 0.13 x 0.062 holes cut through BOTH cap steps -- 0.045 m deep against the first build's 0.03 -- at x +-0.62, with dark floors 2 mm above the body top. Visible at 0, 90, 180, 270 and the hero.

reviewHistory.summary: Surface pass: pinholes, tyre scuffs, a form seam and cloud mottling on one 512 px grime canvas at bump 0.0016; measured rendered spread 11.0/19.1/31.5 against the plate's 12.3/21.6/35.0.

Lighting pass: no rim light and no contact shadow in the plate; both recorded absent. The tonal ladder capping/upper face/slope reproduces within 1.3% and the normalised row profile within 0.08 over 12 bands. Exposure 1.0, ACES filmic.
Interaction pass: ONE root pivot, ZERO sockets, one BOX collider on the body root, no destruction groups.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope 2.036 x 0.80 x 0.60 m (12 mm key tongue included); section from the proxy half-depth profile scaled 0.60/0.66, band table mean |delta width| 0.024, |delta depth| 0.036 H with the residual in the foot bands (the DECLARED depth). The silhouette now carries what the plate's does and the first build's did not: three notches cut through the toe, a capping that overhangs the upper face by 14 mm and steps back at its own top edge, and a chamfer on the bottom arris, the lip break and the slope nose.
Two 0.13 x 0.062 holes cut through BOTH cap steps -- 0.045 m deep against the first build's 0.03 -- at x +-0.62, with dark floors 2 mm above the body top. Visible at 0, 90, 180, 270 and the hero.

Three 0.20 m drainage notches at x = -0.66, 0, +0.66, cut to y = 0.070 by extruding the toe in four spans instead of the whole length. They are gaps, not the dark plates 1 mm proud of the lip that the first build painted on: they break the silhouette at all four turntable azimuths and their cut ends and ceiling are real surfaces.

Measured against the plate over matched crops: upper face renders luma 139.4 sd 11.0 against 139.6 sd 12.3; lower slope 159.3 sd 19.1 against 157.3 sd 21.6; capping 178.3 sd 31.5 against 177.5 sd 35.0. The normalised row profile tracks the plate's over 12 bands within 0.08. The first build rendered the face at 146.7 with sd 5.9 -- right hue, half the spread. The spread is made of 900 air-bubble pinholes at ~1 mm, 11 swept tyre scuffs over the 0.13-0.44 height band, one form seam per 0.8 m and 44 cloud patches.
featureReviews.notes: The plate's chipped end corner is deliberately not modelled: the segment tiles end to end.

reviewHistory.summary: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.94. 272/4,000 triangles, 1/4 draw calls, 1/3 materials, 1/6 unique geometries, one 512 px canvas at 1.3 MB.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the large class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: One component, no repetition system: 1 of 4.

materials.note: concrete only: 1 of 3; the pale top and dark recesses are vertex colours.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 272 of 4,000: two section extrusions split at the nose, four toe spans, two pocketed cap steps, four boxes.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: Two extruded Jersey section parts along X split at the slope nose, four toe spans between the notches, two plan-with-holes extrusions for the pocketed capping; boxes for the pocket floors, key tongue and groove.
No InstancedMesh: the four remaining boxes are one merge. In a scene the HOST instances the whole segment along the median.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.
The material is declared textureless. One 512 px grime canvas after construction at bump 0.0016, 1.3 MB of texture VRAM.

risks.description: The declared 0.60 m foot is 0.06 m narrower than the proxy reads.
risks.mitigation: The declared envelope is the contract; the section shape is the proxy's, scaled by 0.60/0.66, and the band table shows the residual is confined to the foot bands.

risks.description: The pockets are 0.045 m visual recesses; from a low angle their floor is hidden and they read as dark rectangles.
risks.mitigation: Correct: that is what a lifting pocket looks like at prop distance.

risks.description: The grime tile repeats 2.5 times along the 2.00 m length, so any mark larger than about a fifth of the tile is visibly repeated.
risks.mitigation: The cloud mottling was cut from 0.22-0.62 of the tile to 0.04-0.17 for exactly this: at the larger size it read as camouflage with the seam showing. Nothing on the tile is now large enough to recognise twice.
